messages:
marta: pushed a canary of the pos-enc kernel that changes exponent handling for the ROPE+ALiBi combo — tagging eng-runtime. saw one of the perf jobs blow up with infs in attention scores
kevin: CI job https://ci.internal/1856/job/posenc-expon/45 failed with NaNs in attention_qk, logs attached
marta: stack looks like runtime/attention_kernel.cpp:143 compute_scores -> expf overflow. suspect exponent shift when ALiBi slope added on top of rotary scaling
oliver: reproduced locally on T4 + PyTorch 2.2 + AMP. short repro attached, fails with seq_len=2048 and dtype=bf16
marta: repro snippet:
```
python -m tests.repro_posenc --model tiny --seq 2048 --dtype bf16 --pos rope_alibi --seed 42
```
jess: immediate mitigation: clamp logits before exp or use log-sum-exp stable path. Both affect perf/behavior — need careful eval
rahul: agree, prefer doing max-subtract (scores -= max(scores,-1,keepdim=True)) in the kernel — numerically stable and keeps ranking intact
kevin: lse trick is standard but adds an extra reduction per head. rough perf hit measured?
marta: benchmarked quicky — ~2.7% tail-latency increase for 1-token responses on our canary machine. prevents NaNs entirely. tradeoff seems acceptable for hosted default
oliver: also root cause note: ROPE rotation can amplify magnitude with position index; combining with ALiBi linear slope occasionally pushes logits into overflow for bf16 on long seqs. we should bound the combined exponent range
jess: we already have quant profiles recommending lower slopes for bf16+long sequences. maybe kernel should auto-saturate ALiBi slope based on dtype+seq_len rather than forcing app-level changes
rahul: proposal: add a kernel-selector flag 'posenc_numerical_mode' with modes: 'preserve_rank' (current, faster), 'force_stable' (apply lse/clamp + slope-saturation). default preserve_rank for dedicated/private but hosted can default to force_stable
kevin: +1. Also need a perf matrix showing delta per model/seq/dtype so customers understand impact
marta: action items: 1) add lse path behind selector, 2) implement slope cap heuristic (cap = c / sqrt(seq_len) for bf16 maybe), 3) add fuzz CI generating high-slope long-seq combos, 4) telemetry when auto-switch happens
oliver: adding fuzz CI will catch extremes quickly. I'll add a tiny harness that mutates slope and seq_len randomly and asserts no NaNs for attention scores
jess: also run a generation eval on our regression prompt set to assert rank-preservation (bleu-like similarity + manual spot-check)
deploy-bot: canary deployed to canary-1 with route=2% for posenc_numerical_mode change
kevin: I'll open the RFC follow-up PR with perf numbers, toggles, and rollout plan. assigning to @jess for evals
marta: please add a short migration note for Dedicated customers — they may want preserve_rank for cost-sensitive workloads
oliver: one more: add a small flag in kernel telemetry to count how often slope-saturation hits, so we can see prevalence in production
marta: added to checklist in the PR description
ci-bot: created issue #4321 and uploaded logs/artifacts from CI run, linked the canary job
marta: thanks all — if PR lands and no regressions in 24h we'll promote to stable. closing thread.
